scope: Engineering endpoint reconciliation under newly approved reverse polygon-pair construction. These are disclosed edit budgets, not source accuracy tolerances or legal endpoint certification. Original files remain immutable.
common_rules: Fix the newer treaty core endpoints; move only the old engineering candidate endpoint to its corresponding treaty endpoint. Do not displace the full old line or the treaty core to improve apparent agreement.

Use minimum endpoint-only snap first (replace first/last vertex). If it creates a short artificial kink, a local taper may affect ONLY the last/first short segment and must save all displaced vertices, maximum displacement and affected arclength. Do not invent a long smoothing reach.

Intersection count zero is not a stop condition: snap semantically matched source endpoints, then polygonize the paired old/new lines. Result is an engineering closed patch, not independently surveyed legal parcel.

For the country-polygon splice, use exactly the same snapped/shared edge on both countries; validate conservation of their union, no new overlap/gap, valid rings, and unchanged exterior. Source-pair snapping does NOT itself define how the patch attaches to a generalized current baseline.

Do not extend the new effective date backwards from map publication. Label pre-effective reverse output as conditional historic reconstruction; terrain/publication dates are not legal interval bounds.
